videos.script: A member asks to borrow a fourth book. The answer depends on three things, and the program has to choose. This lesson is about choosing. {{if}} First if and else, and the operators that join conditions. One of them skips its right-hand side when the answer is already known, and that matters more than it sounds. {{braces}} Then a bug that compiles: two indented lines that look like one block, and are not. {{switch}} Then the classic switch, where a case is a label to jump to and not a box. Forget one break and two shelves get the same book. {{expressions}} Last, the switch that Java has written since version 14. It produces a value, it never falls through, and since 21 it can ask what type an object is. By the end you can write a decision in the form that cannot fall through, and read the old form when you meet it.
